Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-18
Time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Raj (Verdant Head of ML), Ethan Brooks (Infra), Sofia Nguyen (Security), Liam O'Connor (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Purpose: scope a 4-week pilot: security/compliance gating, workload sizing, benchmarks, and acceptance criteria.
- Key asks: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML support, RBAC/audit logs, sample traffic and golden prompts.
- Outcome: agree pilot timeline, Diego to propose sizing/benchmarks, customer to share traffic and success metrics.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to walk through the pilot scope. diego and i will mostly cover sizing and the bench plan, and we'll collect the security asks up front.
[00:18] Priya (Verdant): great thanks, we have a quick agenda - security checklist, expected workload, and what acceptance looks like. we don't have time to spin up anything fancy yet so we want clear gates.
[00:30] Diego (Redwood SE): perfect. quick clar - are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the pilot? that changes the security path.
[00:40] Ethan (Verdant Infra): short term hosted is fine but we need VPC peering and option to move to dedicated after pilot. we also need SSO/SAML and SCIM for user sync.
[00:53] Sofia (Security): and SOC 2 + ISO 27001 attestation, plus RBAC, fine grained audit logs, and ability to copy logs to our SIEM. also KMS integration or HSM notes for key mgmt.
[01:10] Maya: ok that's clear. we have SOC 2 report and ISO letter we can share, and our platform supports customer-managed keys via KMS or H-S-M — sorry the auto transcript sometimes does K-M-S H-M-S — but yes HSM options exist on private deployments.
[01:30] Liam (Product): for acceptance criteria, Priya and i sketched this: P95 latency under 600ms for chat flows, <200ms for embeddings ops, and accuracy on our 500 eval prompts comparable to baseline model within 2% roc. also cost per 1M tokens under a threshold.
[01:50] Priya: yea accuracy and latency are both key. also we need deterministic audit trails for any data the model sees, and a deletion workflow for PII on request.
[02:05] Diego: notes — so benchmarks should include latency p50/p95/p99, throughput (qps), and quality regression on your eval set. we usually run synthetic load plus replay of your sample traffic. what are your traffic shapes?
[02:22] Priya: rough numbers: 10 qps steady, burst to 180-220 qps during peak, avg seq length around 256 tokens for chat, long tails to 1k for doc summarization but those are rare.
[02:38] Ethan: also we'd like to test cold-starts and KV cache warmup behaviour — we saw differences in other vendors where prefix caching changed p95 dramatically.
[02:52] Diego: yep we'll include KV cache/cold vs warm cache tests. for hardware, we typically propose A10G for cost-sensitive and H100 for latency-sensitive loads. batch sizes will be tuned based on your latency SLO.
[03:10] Maya: and on the compliance front - we can run pilot in private (VPC) if you want isolated network and we can enable SSO/SAML + SCIM. audit logs export to your S3 or to a SIEM via syslog is possible.
[03:24] Sofia: how about retention? we need logs for 1 year and model input retention should be configurable.
[03:31] Diego: retention configurable on dedicated/private. hosted has default retention policy but we can negotiate extended retention for enterprise pilots.
[03:40] Liam: ok good. timeline?
[03:44] Maya: propose 4-week pilot: week 0 (kickoff/security review & runbook), week1 (ingest traffic samples + baseline run), week2 (benchmarks + regressions), week3 (tuning, reruns) and week4 (wrap, acceptance). goal to run initial bench within 10 working days.
[04:04] Priya: that works. we need the bench plan before we commit to dates — like what exact prompts, dataset locations and success thresholds.
[04:12] Diego: i'll draft the benchmark plan. plan will include: 1) synthetic traffic generator matching your qps distribution, 2) replay harness of provided logs, 3) eval runner for your 500 golden prompts, and 4) cost estimates per config.
[04:28] Priya: can you also include tokenization differences between models and a standard pre/post-processing wrapper so our accuracy comparisons are apples-to-apples?
[04:36] Diego: yes, we'll share a dockerized eval runner. note that quantization affects accuracy so we'll list quantization profiles recommended for each hardware option.
[04:46] Ethan: regarding network: how do we verify VPC peering and egress controls during pilot? we have strict egress rules.
[04:53] Maya: for VPC we do a control-plane handshake and only route inference traffic through your VPC or a peered subnet. we can sign an NDA and provide network diagrams.
[05:05] Sofia: audit logs need to show user-level identifiers (SSO id) and request-level metadata incl. model version, prompt hash, and response id.
[05:17] Diego: we can include user_id, route, model_version, latency, token counts, and a prompt-hash field; note that transcription might call it a prompt-hash but it's basically an HMAC.
[05:29] Priya: also need to know how model rollouts will be handled — can we pin versions or do canary splits?
[05:36] Maya: yes version pinning, canary deploys, and automatic fallback to smaller/older variants if latencies spike. all configurable per-route in the console.
[05:48] Liam: on legal/contract gating — aside from SOC2/ISO, we need export control and data residency language in the SOW.
[05:57] Maya: noted. i'll loop in legal after we sign the loa.
[06:02] Priya: for the bench acceptance, propose pass criteria: 1) P95 below target (you'll set config), 2) no more than 2% regression in accuracy against baseline, 3) reproducible runs on at least 2 consecutive days.
[06:20] Diego: that's reasonable. we'll also include flaky test flags for long-tail sequences and specify error budgets.
[06:28] Maya: quick question on competitors — you mentioned you trialed vendor X, anything that failed that we should watch?
[06:33] Priya: with vendor X we saw degraded KV cache performance and opaque pricing on bursts. transparency on per-token and per-embedding cost is a must.
[06:45] Diego: understood. we'll include a detailed cost breakdown per config in the bench report.
[06:52] Sofia: final security q: how do we handle data deletion requests for training/retention?
[06:57] Maya: we support deletion at request and we can run a scrub workflow on private/dedicated deployments; on hosted we support deletion APIs and documented processes.
[07:08] Priya: ok great. lets recap next steps and owners.
[07:12] Maya: recap: maya send SOC2/ISO and security questionnaire; diego send bench plan + sizing; priya send traffic samples and eval prompts; we aim to kick off week of 2026-03-22.
[07:24] Liam: sounds good. can you also add a short list of sample instance configs and expected cost per day?
[07:30] Diego: yes i'll include A10G baseline and H100 low-latency runs with expected cost and token throughput.
[07:36] Priya: thanks everyone.
[07:38] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with doc links.

End of transcript.
